headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if Pathway outputs are fed into the system_prompts_leaks corpus, but the pair is otherwise mostly isolated by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing agent with no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or network surfaces, while system_prompts_leaks is a source-available corpus about prompt leaks. A direct injection path is not documented, so only manual copy/paste or external bridging would let Pathway content influence B.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Pathway output into the system_prompts_leaks workflow, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile is later given a shared filesystem or MCP bridge, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Do not copy raw Pathway output into B without sanitizing.
Disable any shared clipboard or workspace bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows shared storage, file access, or outbound network. Pathway cannot read or write files, and system_prompts_leaks only advertises network egress none. With no shared workspace or upload path, there is no plausible data-leakage route between them.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is introduced, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains outbound upload capability, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway has no write, shell, git, or network capabilities, and system_prompts_leaks exposes no write surfaces at all. Without overlapping mutable resources, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk changes.
IF shared mutable OAuth or git state is added, reassess.
mitigations: Document any future write scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: system_prompts_leaks could treat Pathway-generated text as material for analysis, but Pathway is a document processor and not an action-taking agent. The pair lacks a documented default chain where B blindly executes A's outputs, so the main risk is mistaken attribution during manual review.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat Pathway output as authoritative instructions, cascading error risk rises.
IF Pathway output is auto-ingested into a downstream action pipeline, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Label Pathway output as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add verification checksums or provenance metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling fields are present for either profile, and both are docs-only with no touched data classes. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, no specific compliance mismatch is evidenced here.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are added, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until policies are defined.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the profiles.
